input.question: If I traveled to space in a space ship that remained completely stationary, would I age faster than those on earth?
input.ground_truth: Due to special relativity, "completely stationary" doesn't make sense. In your reference frame, you would be stationary, so you would age faster. To someone on Earth, the planet would be stationary, so people on Earth would age faster.

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you and your friend are both holding a toy clock. You get into a magic spaceship that doesn’t move at all—it just stays in the same spot in space, like you’re standing still.

Now, your friend stays on Earth, playing and watching their clock.

Here’s the thing: If your spaceship doesn’t move at all and isn’t near any big planets or stars, time for you and your friend on Earth will tick at almost the same speed. But if you go really, really far away from Earth, or if you go super fast (even if you’re not moving, but just being in a strong gravity place), time can tick a little bit differently for you and your friend. This is called “relativity,” which is a big word scientists use.

But if your spaceship just sits perfectly still and doesn’t go fast or near a big planet, you and your friend will both get older at almost the same speed! So, you won’t get older faster just because you’re in space and they’re on Earth, as long as you both stay still and nothing else changes.
